solution: The Security Council section lists the five permanent members exactly: "America, Russia, England, France and China are permanent members of the Security Council. They have the veto power." Germany is the only option absent from that list, so it is the odd one out. (The chapter's closing note that India is seeking permanent membership underlines that the list of five is closed.)

The 'Do you know?' box says: "UNICEF is an affiliated organisation of the United Nations. It works towards making nutritious food and health care available to children. Several workshops were organised in India to find out measures to overcome malnutrition among babies and children." UNESCO is the rival, but the same box confines it to education, science and culture; the Trusteeship Council's work ended in 1994 and the Red Cross is not a UN body at all.

Under 'The Objectives of the United Nations' the chapter says: "In the beginning, only 50 countries were members of the United Nations. Today, this number has gone up to 193." The figure 50 also appears as the number of countries that drafted the Charter at San Francisco; none of 190, 198 or 199 appears anywhere in the chapter.
